blocks.text: A2-03 · The complete indicative imperfection
Lesson overview

The imperfect ( ⁧المُضَارِع⁩ ) is the time of habits, actions in progress and descriptions: "What do you usually do" , "What happens now , but also the headlines at present. In A1 You used it with regular verbs. Here you complete the picture: all people with duals, the prefix in u-, verbs with hamza and, above all, weak verbs, who change to the imperfect more than perfect. The rule of the two bases of A2-02 It's worth it here too. Two weeks.

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-03), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. conjugate to the imperfect a regular verb in all persons, including duals and 'voi / their females;
2. choose the ya- or yu- prefix according to the verb type;
3. combine verbs with hamza ( ⁧يَأْخُذُ⁩ , ⁧يَقْرَأُ⁩ ) and those with ⁧و⁩ initial ( ⁧يَصِلُ⁩ , ⁧يَجِدُ⁩ , ⁧يَضَعُ⁩ );
4. conjugate concave verbs ( ⁧يَقُولُ⁩ , ⁧يَبِيعُ⁩ , ⁧يَنَامُ⁩ ) and defects ( ⁧يَمْشِي⁩ , ⁧يَدْعُو⁩ , ⁧يَنْسَى⁩ ), plus ⁧يَأْتِي⁩ and ⁧يَرَى⁩ ;
5. use the imperfect for habits, ongoing actions and nearby programs, with frequency adverbs;
6. understand newspaper titles without vowels built with the imperfect;
7. describe your day and week in 100 words and voice for two minutes.
Two-week plan.

2. The imperfect in all people
The imperfect prefixes (in all people) and, in some people, suffixes. Conjugation complete of ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ :
They (f.) ⁧يَدْرُسْنَهُنَّ⁩ yadrusna
Three comments you need for the entire form.
1. The prefix ta- has five uses (you m., she, you two, them two f., you): without context ⁧تَدْرُسُ⁩ may be studies or studies. In the texts it decides the subject expressed or the context.

2. The -u terminations, -īna, -āni, -ūna are the sign of the sign. In conjunction (A2-04) and in the jurissive (A2-05) will change: the -u becomes -a or disappears, and the -na / -ni final falls. Learn how to see these endings as a piece apart: tadrus- īna , yadrus- āni , yadrus- ūna .

3. -na of .../they (f.) is not a termination of the indication: it is the sign of the female plural, and remains in all the ways. In front of -na the base has no final vowel (yadrus-na): like the perfect, it is a suffix that begins with a consonant. In pause the final -u falls (adrus, yadrus); terminations -īna, -āni, -ūna are pronounced -īn, -ān, -ūn.
3. The prefix: ya- or yu-?

rows: simple verb (form I) and forms with t- or st- before root (V, VI, VII, VIII, X)
forms II, III, IV and verbs of four consonants

• ⁧يَدْرُسُ⁩ yadrusu ... ⁧يُدَرِّسُ⁩ yudarrisu
• ⁧يَعْلَمُ⁩ yaʿlamu "Sa" is "sa" ⁧يُعَلِّمُ⁩ yuʿallimu Instruction, instruction and training
4. Verbs with hamza and verbs with ⁧و⁩ initial
With hamza. They're regular. Two particularities:
• Verbs starting with hamza: two hamzees in a row merge into ā long written ⁧آ⁩ : ⁧أَأْخُذُ⁩ → ⁧آخُذُ⁩
āḫuḏu, ⁧أَأْكُلُ⁩ → ⁧آكُلُ⁩ ākulu;

• the hamza changes support in front of -īna and -ūna: ⁧تَقْرَئِينَ⁩ taqraʾīna, ⁧يَقْرَؤُونَ⁩ yaqraʾūna (also ⁧يَقْرَأُونَ⁩ ). The rules are in A2-16. With ⁧و⁩ initial (verbs .) (assimilated) In form I ⁧و⁩ of the root disappears to the imperfect. It is a regular loss: all people have the basis without ⁧و⁩ .
⁧وَقَعَ⁩ • fall; to be found ⁧يَقَعُ⁩ yaqaʿu ⁧يَقَعُونَأَقَعُ⁩

How do you recognize it in a text: a word like ⁧يصل⁩ seems to have a root of two letters ( ⁧ص ل⁩ ). If you don't find anything in the dictionary with two letters, try one ⁧و⁩ front: ⁧و ص ل⁩ . In derived forms the ⁧و⁩ may remain or assimilate: ⁧يَتَّصِلُ⁩ Call, contact ⁧و ص ل⁩ ( ⁧و⁩ has become ⁧ت⁩ And it doubled: A2-18).
5. Concave verbs to the imperfect
The concave has a long vowel in the center: ū, ī or ā. It is the same vowel that determines the short vowel of the perfect (A2-02Section 5).
ā ⁧نِمْتُيَخَافُ⁩ , ⁧يَنَامُ⁩ ⁧خِفْتُ⁩ ,
The rule of the two bases, to the imperfect. The long vowel remains in almost all people, because almost all suffixes begin with a vowel. The exception is -na of 'voi / loro (f.)
They (f.) ⁧يَقُلْنَ⁩ yaqulna ⁧يَبِعْنَ⁩ yabiʿna ⁧يَنَمْنَ⁩ yanamna
The short forms of "voi" / their (f.) are rare in the texts, but the same reduction will return, much more frequent, to the juxtaposition: ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَكُنْ⁩ ( A2-05).
6. Verbs flawed to the imperfect; ⁧يَأْتِي⁩ and ⁧يَرَى⁩
The flaw of defects ends with a long vowel: ī, ū or ā. The terminations -īna and -ūna They merge with this vowel: learn the three families as tables.
How they form.
• Type ī ( ⁧يَمْشِي⁩ ): -ī + -ūna → -ūna (yamšūna); -ī + -īna → -īna (tamšīna). So: ⁧يَقْضِي⁩ , ⁧يَبْنِي⁩ , ⁧يَشْتَرِي⁩ , ⁧يَنْتَهِي⁩ ,
⁧يُعْطِي⁩ , ⁧يَأْتِي⁩ .
• Type ū ( ⁧يَدْعُو⁩ ): -ū + -īna → -īna (tadʿīna); -ū + -ūna → -ūna (yadʿūna). The forms (m.) and (m.) used (f.) ... ⁧يَدْعُونَ⁩ .
• Type ā ( ⁧يَنْسَى⁩ ): ā becomes diphthong: -ayna, -awna (tansayna, yansawna). So: ⁧يَبْقَى⁩ , ⁧يَلْقَى⁩ , ⁧يَرَى⁩ .

What are in A2-02. The type ī corresponds to the perfect in -ā written ⁧ى⁩ ( ⁧مَشَى⁩ – ⁧يَمْشِي⁩ ), the type ū to the perfect in -ā written ⁧ا⁩ ( ⁧دَعَا⁩ – ⁧يَدْعُو⁩ ), the type ā to the perfect in -iya ( ⁧نَسِيَ⁩ – ⁧يَنْسَى⁩ ). Important exception: ⁧رَأَى⁩ – ⁧يَرَى⁩ .
⁧يَأْتِي⁩ and ⁧يَرَى⁩ , two verbs to know by heart.
⁧يَأْتِي⁩ comes from ⁧أَتَى⁩ (Root ⁧أ ت ي⁩ ): ā as long as ⁧آكُلُ⁩ . In ⁧يَرَى⁩ the root hamza ( ⁧ر أ ي⁩ ) disappears throughout the imperfect: yarā, not *yarʾā.
7. Double verbs to the imperfect

Verbs with second and third equal consonant have double consonant and vowel first: ⁧يَرُدُّ⁩ Yaruddu, ⁧يَمُرُّ⁩ yamuru, ⁧يُحِبُّ⁩ yuḥibbu (prefix u-: is a form IV). All people are regular ( ⁧أَرُدُّ⁩ , ⁧تَرُدِّينَ⁩ , ⁧يَرُدُّونَ⁩ ) except, once again, "voi" (f.), where the two consonants separate: ⁧يَرْدُدْنَ⁩ Yardudna. The detail is in A2-16.
8. The Uses of the Imperfect

rows: I wake up at six every day.
What are you doing now? I'm translating a letter.
The airport is located in the north of the city.
program near (with an expression of time)
In winter the train may be late.

blocks.text: Arabic does not have a progressive present. ⁧أُتَرْجِمُ⁩ is either 'translated' or 'translating'. If you want to point out that the action is ongoing now, add ⁧الآنَ⁩ . The frequency adverbs, from the most to the least frequent: ⁧دَائِمًا⁩ • • • ⁧عَادَةً⁩ Usually, it's a bit of a bit of a bit of a bitch. ⁧غَالِبًا⁩ Mostly, often, often. ⁧كَثِيرًا⁩ Often, very often · ⁧أَحْيَانًا⁩ "Sometimes" · ⁧نَادِرًا⁩ • • • rarely • ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧أَبَدًا⁩ "Never..." They are usually put after the verb or at the bottom of the sentence: ⁧أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ دَائِمًا⁩ , ⁧لَا أَشْرَبُ القَهْوَةَ أَبَدًا⁩ . The expressions of time to the accusative: ⁧كُلَّ يَوْمٍ⁩ • every day • • ⁧كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ⁩ , ⁧صَبَاحًا⁩ , ⁧مَسَاءً⁩ , ⁧لَيْلًا⁩ , ⁧نَهَارًا⁩ , ⁧يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ⁩ , ⁧يَوْمِيًّا⁩ daily.
9. Titles without vowels
In news headlines and subtitles, the imperfect indicates present or imminent action. To read them without vowels, he uses three clues:
1. the prefix says the person: ⁧يـ⁩ = he (or their) with - ⁧ون⁩ ), ⁧تـ⁩ = she, that is a female subject, often an institution ( ⁧الشرطة تبحث⁩ "The police are looking for" or a plural of things;
2. the subject usually comes before the verb in the title: ⁧الرئيس يزور⁩ …;
3. the preposition that follows the verb helps you to understand which verb is: ⁧تبحث عن⁩ "Search" means: ⁧يتصل بـ⁩ • contact:
⁧يصل إلى⁩ It's going to get to the top.

rows: The police are looking for a stolen car.

blocks.text: 10. Pronunciation

-īna, -ūna, -āni. They're long vowels: tadrusīna, yadrusūna, yadrusāni. Pause: tadrusīn, yadrusūn, yadrusān. Do not shorten them: "tadrusin" sounds like a mistake. Prefix a- / u-. adrusu \'studio Â" and udarrisu Â's teacherÂ's are already distinguished from the first vowel: trained with the B script. The diphthongs of defects. tansayna, yansawna: ay come in "mai" , aw come in "Auto" . The type ū has vowels as well: tadʿīna, yadʿūna. ⁧آ⁩ = ʾā. ⁧آكُلُ⁩ is pronounced with the blow of glottis and the ā long: ʾākulu.
